mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.25% (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as lower rates reduce discount rates for equity valuations and stimulate risk-taking.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS < 0.25% predicting positive 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.50% (FEDFUNDS > 0.50%) signals monetary tightening that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.50% (based on historical data from 2000-2020).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE < 5.0%) and increase in employment (PAYEMS > 140,000 thousand) signals a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the joint signal (UNRATE decline and PAYEMS increase) predicting positive 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (characterized by high consumer spending), rising housing starts (HOUST > 1100 thousand units) predict positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to increased construction activity and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1100 and the economy is in a late-cycle expansion (as defined by high GDP growth and low unemployment).

mechanism_narrative: In a post-pandemic recovery regime (characterized by low inflation and high unemployment), a decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the central bank supports economic recovery.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS < 0.25% predicting positive 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window during the post-pandemic recovery period.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate above 5.0% (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals economic weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% (based on historical data from 2000-2020).

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST > 1100 thousand units) are associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as increased construction activity boosts consumer confidence and spending across the economy.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for HOUST > 1100 predicting positive 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (INDPRO < 100) signals a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain disruptions that reduce corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100 (based on historical data from 2000-2020).
